subject.title: [Feature]: feat: trigger session-memory hook on /compact command

question: Should bundled session-memory archive on compaction, and should that use the existing `session:compact:before` lifecycle event rather than a new `command:compact` trigger?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects hook API shape, automatic versus manual compaction coverage, transcript retention, and write frequency, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Use pre-compaction lifecycle
options.body: Approve session-memory capture on `session:compact:before` with explicit context payload, bounded async behavior, docs, and tests.

options.title: Add command-only compact trigger
options.body: Only manual `/compact` would archive, leaving automatic compaction to the existing plugin lifecycle hooks.

options.title: Defer to continuity or memoryFlush
options.body: Keep session-memory command-scoped and require newer continuity/memoryFlush work to own compaction-time preservation.

recommendation.title: Use pre-compaction lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve session-memory capture on `session:compact:before` with explicit context payload, bounded async behavior, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current compaction lifecycle hook surface that the proposed behavior should reuse or consciously avoid.
